title: Used EV buying guide: The $30,000 edition
gist: Used EV prices have risen just over 5 percent since February despite growing ex-lease supply, because a new US war in the Middle East pushed demand into electrics; Cox Automotive data show used EV sales up roughly 20 percent year over year and only 38 days' supply versus 81 for new EVs. The $25,000–$30,000 band now holds over 9,000 listings dominated by Tesla, Hyundai Ioniq 5, Chevrolet Blazer/Equinox EV and Ford Mustang Mach-E, with residual-value tells visible in which brands have collapsed to that price.

themes.theme: Used EV pricing decoupled from supply

insights.claim: Used EV prices have risen just over 5 percent since February even as ex-lease supply keeps increasing, with the author attributing the demand shift to America's latest war in the Middle East and its effect on fuel costs.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: EV residual values now behave like a levered call on oil geopolitics — a support for lessors' book values and for OEM captive finance arms that had been writing down EV residuals.
insights.quote: As a result of America’s latest war in the Middle East, used EVs have appreciated by just over 5 percent since February.
insights.locator: A strange thing is happening in the used EV market

insights.claim: Cox Automotive data show used EV sales were up 25 percent year over year through May, with a weaker June trimming the full-year pace to just over 20 percent growth.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Twenty-percent volume growth alongside rising prices is the strongest combination for dealer gross margin — a positive read for used-vehicle retailers with EV inventory.
insights.quote: used EV sales have been strong this year—up 25 percent year over year by May, although a weaker June has brought overall sales up just over 20 percent year over year
insights.locator: A strange thing is happening in the used EV market

insights.claim: Cox Automotive measured 38 days' supply of used EVs in June versus 81 days for new EVs, meaning used electrics turn more than twice as fast as new ones.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: The bottleneck in EV adoption is new-vehicle price, not consumer appetite — new-EV inventory at 81 days points to continued incentive spending and margin pressure for OEMs.
insights.quote: just 38 days’ supply of used EVs in June, but 81 days for new EVs
insights.locator: Used EVs also hang around on dealer lots

insights.claim: Analysts at Recurrent report that much of the used EV demand sits at the cheaper end of the price spectrum, and Autotrader shows more than 9,000 used EVs listed between $25,000 and $30,000.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: The volume market for electrics is now sub-$30,000 used, which structurally disadvantages OEMs whose EV lineups start above $40,000 new.
insights.locator: And much of the demand is at the cheaper end

insights.claim: Used EVs priced at or below $25,000 may now qualify for a $1,750 rebate in California, adding a state-level subsidy to the cheapest tier of the used market.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Subsidy support has migrated from new to used EVs at the state level, creating a price cliff at $25,000 that shapes where inventory clears fastest.
insights.locator: In previous installments of our used EV buyers’ guide

themes.theme: Which nameplates dominate the sub-$30k inventory

insights.claim: Chevrolet supplies roughly 750 Blazer EVs and 550 Equinox EVs in the $25,000–$30,000 used band, with the Equinox EV starting new at not much more, implying used examples are low-mileage and well-specced.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: GM's mass-market EVs are depreciating into near-new-price territory, compressing the spread between new and used and cannibalizing new-vehicle sales.

insights.claim: Hyundai's E-GMP models remain recommendable despite ICCU reliability fears because the automaker extended the ICCU warranty to 15 years or 180,000 miles, with over 1,000 Ioniq 5s available in the price band versus half as many Kia EV6s.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: An extended warranty is Hyundai buying back residual value — an explicit, quantifiable cost of a component defect that other OEMs will face as EV fleets age.
insights.quote: the automaker recently extended the ICCU warranty to 15 years/180,000 miles, so we still feel comfortable recommending its E-GMP-based EVs
insights.locator: Although Hyundai’s ICCU reliability has commenters running

insights.claim: Tesla's enormous EV market share translates into thousands of used Teslas available in the $25,000–$30,000 range, far more than any other single brand.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Tesla's installed base sets the clearing price for the entire sub-$30k used EV segment, so its residuals drive competitors' pricing power.
insights.quote: Given Tesla’s enormous market share for EVs, it’s no surprise that you’ll find thousands of them for sale, used, in our price range.

insights.claim: Neither the Chevrolet Blazer EV nor the Equinox EV supports Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, a deal-breaker for many buyers, while the closely related Honda Prologue is essentially the same vehicle with CarPlay included.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: GM's decision to drop phone projection is visible as a demand discount in the used market — a direct read on whether owning the infotainment stack is worth the lost sales.
insights.quote: There are also a couple hundred Honda Prologues, which are essentially the Chevy Blazer EV but with Apple CarPlay.
insights.locator: You’ll have to look a bit harder

insights.claim: Nissan Ariyas and Volkswagen ID.4s each show roughly 400 used units in the band, while Toyota bZ4x and Subaru Solterra appear in similar volumes but only as older models with CCS1 ports and less-efficient first-generation powertrains.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: First-generation powertrains and CCS1 charge ports are becoming an identifiable obsolescence tier in used EV pricing as the market shifts to NACS.
insights.locator: There are about the same number of used Nissan Ariyas

themes.theme: Brand exit and reliability as residual-value signals

insights.claim: Polestar has exited the US market, which depresses buyer confidence in used Polestar 2s even though the cars can still be serviced at Volvo dealers.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Market exit imposes an immediate residual-value discount independent of product quality — a cost OEMs should weigh before retrenching from a region.
insights.quote: The latter is now from an OEM that has exited the US market, which may well put some people off, but the cars can be serviced at Volvo dealers, so don’t be scared.
insights.locator: Sedan lovers should consider the Hyundai Ioniq 6

insights.claim: Vinfast VF8s, Jaguar I-Paces and Jeep Wagoneer Ses have depreciated into the sub-$30,000 range and are flagged as vehicles to avoid, with the Vinfast and Jeep named among the worst EVs the author has driven.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Steep depreciation into bargain-bin territory is the market's verdict on these programs — a leading indicator for write-downs and program cancellations at VinFast, Jaguar and Stellantis.
insights.quote: probably safer to avoid the few Vinfast VF8s and Jaguar I-Paces out there, as well as the handful of Jeep Wagoneer Ses that have depreciated to this price range
insights.locator: How brave/mad do you feel today?

insights.claim: Used Cadillac Lyriqs in the price band are mostly high-mileage ex-livery cars, indicating fleet and ride-hail channels rather than retail buyers absorbed much of that model's early volume.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Fleet-heavy sales mix inflates reported volumes but degrades used-market pricing later — a quality-of-earnings check on OEM EV delivery numbers.
insights.locator: Less common options that still come with a fancy badge

insights.claim: Nearly new Nissan Leafs and Chevrolet Bolt EUVs appear in the used band while both models are also available new for under $30,000 — the current Leaf below $30,000 excluding destination and a new LFP-pack Bolt under $30,000 — leaving almost no used-versus-new discount.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: When new LFP-based EVs price at par with two-year-old used stock, the entry-level used market loses its arbitrage and cheap-new EVs take that demand.
insights.locator: You’ll also find some very nearly new Nissan Leafs

insights.claim: Flagship luxury EVs have collapsed to the $30,000 level in small numbers — eight Mercedes-Benz EQSs, one Lucid Air Grand Touring, one Audi e-Tron GT and one Porsche Taycan 4S — with servicing bills still matching cars that cost four times as much new.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Luxury EV depreciation is brutal and now visible in listings, which undermines the leasing economics and pricing power of premium EV programs at Mercedes, Porsche and Lucid.
insights.locator: For the really brave, you might even slip into one

insights.claim: BrightDrop delivery vans have depreciated into the sub-$30,000 used range in meaningful numbers, and Ford F-150 Lightning Pro work-spec trucks are also reachable at that price with patience.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Commercial EV residuals are weak, raising the total-cost-of-ownership hurdle for fleet electrification and pressuring GM's BrightDrop and Ford's Pro business cases.
insights.locator: And then there are the real rarities
